title: Principality of Salerno
capsule: The Principality of Salerno was formed in 851 when Siconulf split from the Principality of Benevento, establishing an independent Lombard state on the Tyrrhenian coast of southern Italy with Salerno as its capital. Under Guaimar IV (1027–1052) the principality reached its greatest extent, controlling most of continental southern Italy and cultivating the Schola Medica Salernitana, regarded as the earliest medical school in medieval Europe. Gisulf II's weak reign alienated his Norman allies, and in 1077 Robert Guiscard besieged and captured Salerno, ending Lombard rule and incorporating the city into the Norman Duchy of Apulia and Calabria.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory around Salerno and the Lombard principalities is well documented in chronicles and charters; precise border fluctuations with Capua and Benevento require reconstruction from fragmentary narrative sources.
